audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 4-5, 6 and first item read Urgot and the last row reads Skill, which disagrees with the already-audited mirror.
audit.why: The mirror (gragas__urgot) set the chart, as one atomic group across both layers, to Skill / Urgot / Urgot / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Urgot. Those tokens are champion names, so they read identically from either side; matching them is what keeps the two pages from rendering opposite answers, and mirror-fix would overwrite any disagreement anyway. Both layers are proposed together, plus the phase whys and content whys that would otherwise contradict the new sides.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Urgot / Urgot / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Urgot with ratings rescaled and every affected why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Body Slam is named on nearly every line with no cooldown attached.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, Barrel Roll 10/9/8/7/6s at 850 range, Drunken Rage 5s, Explosive Cask 100/85/70s at 1000 range. Yours: Purge 12s down to no cooldown and no cost at rank 5 inside 490 range, Disdain 16s at rank 1, Fear Beyond Death 100/85/70s.
audit.corrected: Body Slam's 14s now anchors the commit advice, and the range gap (his 850 Barrel Roll versus your 490 Purge) explains the mid-lane rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentions that Drunken Rage is a 1-second sample ending in an auto-attack reset, nor that Happy Hour heals him off every cast.
audit.why: The sample is a channel with a visible wind-up: the mirror already establishes that Disdain cuts it, so the flip must go out while he is drinking, not after. And because the combo ends in an auto reset, the wind-up rather than the cast is the cue to step back. Happy Hour's periodic heal on skill use is why chip damage without Grievous Wounds leaks value.
audit.corrected: report[5].t now states the sample interrupt; the anti-heal purchase was already correct in report[8].

audit.why: report[8] already prescribes Executioner's Calling on the first back, which is the right answer to Happy Hour's repeated healing.

edits.after: Both ults land at 6, but Explosive Cask knocks you out of Purge range while Fear Beyond Death needs him low before it does anything.

edits.after: Black Cleaver stacks fast with W, but his first item buys resistances and Drunken Rage's damage reduction blunts the spike. Trade short.

edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out — Barrel Roll out-ranges you and Happy Hour heals the chip.

edits.after: Level 6 goes to him — Explosive Cask knocks you out of Purge range before you shred.

edits.after: First item favours him: resistances and cask displacement blunt your spike.

edits.after: With 2+ items the head-on duel is yours again — Cleaver and Sterak's out-grind his displacement.

edits.before: Track Gragas's Body Slam: His engage. Bait it, then shred. When it is down — W-shred him.

edits.before: This flips to Gragas: with items his Cask displacement and Body Slam engage give him teamfight utility that out-ranges your immobile frame, and he can peel you off carries or knock you away from your R target.
edits.after: Late this swings back to you in a straight fight: Cleaver and Sterak's grind through Drunken Rage's damage reduction, and once he has spent Body Slam and Explosive Cask he has nothing left to keep you off him.

edits.before: At first item you're still ahead and should press for plates and roams. But with 2+ items the matchup swings to Gragas: his Explosive Cask and Body Slam give him fight-altering displacement that plays around your immobility, letting him peel you off your R target or knock you out of position when your team commits.
edits.after: At first item he is the more comfortable one: resistances and Happy Hour blunt your chip while Explosive Cask keeps you off him at 1000 range. With 2+ items it swings back — Cleaver and Sterak's grind through his damage reduction, and once Body Slam and Cask are spent he has no way to keep you out of Purge range.
